notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already spent when this part began (its one search was refused: 200 of 200 used), so nothing here comes from a search engine and none was read in place of the search tool. Every page was opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), one request at a time and at least a second apart on any one site, with each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed: the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (learned by running the kit's own step, python -m ballot.local_sites files, on a scratch copy of the database; the real database was only read; 16 of these 30 candidates filed one), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates and local party units' sites, the Legislative Reference Library, the University of Minnesota's election archive by a candidate's own address (it has a page for Steve Simon and for nobody else here), Wikipedia's article pages, and three news organizations whose robots.txt lets a reader in (KAXE, Woodbury News Net, the Fairmont Sentinel). The own search pages of a few more were asked and gave nothing (Lakeland PBS, KFGO, KYMN, Sahan Journal, the Dodge County Independent). About 185 pages were asked for, and about 130 robots.txt files, nearly all on the evening of October 1, 2026 and the last few in the first minutes of October 2. A campaign site nobody filed could only be found where a party page links it or a likely address exists, so a missing website here is not proof that none exists.

A rule this part held itself to, and a question for John: a site was left alone when its robots.txt shuts out the kit's own name or any of Anthropic's named agents (ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai), since this sweep is run by Claude. Parts 16, 17 and 23 did the same; other parts read some of these sites under the kit's own name, which their robots.txt allows. The rule closed to this part: hometownsource.com (the Sun papers, the Press & News, the Union-Times), presspubs.com, southernminn.com, the Forum Communications papers (Brainerd Dispatch, Bemidji Pioneer, Detroit Lakes Tribune, Post Bulletin), patch.com, minnlawyer.com, kstp.com, minnesotareformer.com, valleynewslive.com, kvrr.com, the FM Extra, the Pine County papers and ramseycounty.us. If John decides the kit's own name is what counts, the races here that those papers would most help are Edina (Scot Housh), New Hope (Jeffrey S. Miller), Osseo (Sarah Mitchell), Woodbury (Anne Burt), the years of Jeff Larson's terms on the Milaca board, and the two judges' appointments. These ask every script to stay out and were not read: benformoorhead.com (the site Ben Livingston filed, so it is not confirmed here and the filed address stands on its own), the City of Detroit Lakes' site, and the search pages of Crow Wing County, MPR News and the Montevideo American-News.

Not read, and nothing worked around: anneburt.com, the site Anne Burt filed (it answered the kit's reader with a bot check, so no website finding is recorded for her and the filed address stands on its own); sd13dfl.org, the Senate District 13 DFL (403; it was asked twice, which was this part's slip: the reader was then changed so that a page that refuses is never asked again); the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site and the state's mn.gov pages (not requested at all, since other parts met a 403 and a CAPTCHA there); the Secretary of State's own sites (never requested); bringmethenews.com's search (403); the Fairmont Sentinel's and Lakes Area Radio's search (their search pages show nothing without scripts, and the sites' own search interfaces answered 401 and 504); the City of Lexington's site (it closed the connection); the Crosby-Ironton district's board page (its address was not found: the site's menu is drawn by script, and two likely addresses were 404). www.co.todd.mn.us and www.belleplaine.k12.mn.us did not answer; the county's and the district's pages are at www.toddcountymn.gov and www.isd716.org.

joemcdonaldmn.com answered the kit's reader with 429 (too many requests) at the first ask. Its robots.txt allows every reader, so its home page and its About page were read with the page-reading tool instead (two requests). That tool summarizes a page, so only the title and the committee line it reported are quoted. The second reader may meet the same 429 with a script and should open the site in a browser.

Pages drawn by script: Jeff Larson's and Ashley Patel's campaign sites and the Mahtomedi district's School Board page show nothing to a plain reader; the words quoted from them are in the script or data the page is drawn from (jefflarsonforhouse.com/assets/index-BZ4Xziak.js, ashleyforshoreview.org/assets/index-C0Qn0Gno.js, and the data inside the Mahtomedi page itself). A person sees the same words by opening the page in a browser. The kit's fetch step may find no photo options or issue headings on the two campaign sites for the same reason.

For the second reader: (a) Joe McDonald is a sitting member with a roster record, so only his website matters by the sweep's rule; three local offices from the Legislative Reference Library's record of him are also given, because the roster does not carry them (the Library gives no years for the school board seat). Drop them if they are not wanted. No Republican party page publishing his 2026 endorsement was found: the Wright County Republicans' site lists him under 'Elected Officials', and its home page calls a convention for the 'Endorsement of Candidates for House and Senate of districts 29 and 30' without giving the result. (b) Steve Simon's record page comes from the roster's statewide officials, which has no birth date and no earlier service; the Library's record of him gives both, and is given as his official page because the Secretary of State's own site is never requested from this machine. A job the Library also lists is left out. His own_words quote joins the heading of his site's Endorsements page and one line of its list with an ellipsis. Three of his four earlier runs under a party label rest on the University of Minnesota's election archive, labelled secondary as other parts label it; the birth details that archive shows were not taken. (c) Scott Winger's birth year is worked out, not printed: KAXE's 2024 guide prints his own answer 'Age on Election Day: 63 it will be my birthday', and Election Day was November 5, 2024, which fixes the year at 1961. Only the year is recorded (part 17 records a year the same way from 'I will celebrate my 60th birthday'). Drop it if a worked-out year is not wanted. Beltrami County writes his term '2024-2026' and writes the terms of the three commissioners elected in November 2024 '2024-2028', so 2024 is read as the election year, not the year he took his seat. (d) Anne Burt: the sources disagree on when she became mayor, so no start year is given. Wikipedia's list of Woodbury's mayors gives her years as 2018 to the present and cites a Pioneer Press story of February 4, 2019 about 'Woodbury's new mayor'; Woodbury News Net wrote on June 27, 2025 that she 'was elected mayor in 2020'. Her filed campaign site could not be read (a bot check); Woodbury News Net's guide to the 2026 candidates links her name to anneburt.com, so a person with a browser can confirm it. The same Woodbury News Net sentence names a 2040 Comprehensive Plan Task Force, left out as an advisory task force, and the story names a regional mayors' association, which is not a public office. (e) Sarah Mitchell's start year, 2023, is worked out: the district says members serve four-year terms and hers 'Expires January 2027', and her own site says she was 'elected in November 2022'. (f) Jeffrey S. Miller: the City of New Hope's Human Rights Commission page lists 'Jeffrey Miller (Chair)', the only Miller on any of the city's four boards and commissions, and his campaign site speaks of 'my current volunteer work as a New Hope City Commissioner'; no page says in so many words that the two are one person. (g) Ashley Patel's campaign site says she served on Shoreview's Human Rights Commission; the city's page for that commission does not list her among today's members, so the office has no years and no end. (h) Gloria Murphy's posts in the City of Lexington rest on her campaign site alone (the city's site would not answer). (i) Kathryn A. Lorsbach: KAXE reported her appointment on November 24, 2024; the Judicial Branch's page could not be read to confirm the day she took the bench or that Seat 14 is hers, so the judgeship has no start year and no end. (j) Jon W. Lubke, David Lieser, Denise Gaida and Reese Frederickson: each county's own page shows the office held today; none says when it began (Crow Wing County gives only 'Current Term: 2023 to 2027'). (k) Krish Subrahmanian is printed as Krishnan Subrahmanian on the state DFL's list. (l) The election archive has no page under the names of Trent C Dilks, Krish Subrahmanian, Jeff Larson or Joe Brothers, so no earlier run under a party label is recorded for them; the state DFL's list links Jeff Larson's name to a social media page, which is not used, and his filed site was read instead.

Read and left out on purpose: employment (jobs are not offices by the sweep's rule; whether a sheriff candidate's card should show police posts from the candidate's own site is a question for John); nonprofit, hospital, school-site and association boards (Scot Housh, Brian R. Mueller, Ashley Patel, Anne Burt, Ana Folpe); on Scot Housh's site an 'Edina Crime Prevention Board', and on Brian R. Mueller's a 'Commissioner - Minnesota Law Enforcement Accreditation' line, neither of which could be confirmed as a government body; party posts (Ana Folpe's own site says she has been an officer of a local DFL unit, which is recorded only as her own words); labor and personal endorsements; ages given without a year (KAXE's Detroit Lakes guide gives Natalie Bly's age on Election Day); schools and graduation years; households. Not opened at all: the affidavits of candidacy and financial reports the City of Moorhead posts for its candidates.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6, 8, 10 and 12 use), two items: the Senate District 43 DFL lists Jeffrey S. Miller under 'Letters of Support', and says in so many words that a letter of support is not a DFL endorsement (parts 8 and 10 record the same page for two other candidates; his own site's words about it are recorded as own_words); and the Olmsted 20/24 DFL's '2026 DFL Voting Guide', a sample ballot its home page links, names Ana Folpe among its choices for the Rochester School Board and calls them recommendations. Both are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision.

For whoever holds the Rochester and Olmsted County races, and for the endorsement ledger (ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json), which has this unit's June newsletter but not this guide: the Olmsted 20/24 DFL's '2026 DFL Voting Guide' (https://olmsted2024dfl.com/s/DFL-voting-guide-2026.pdf, linked from https://olmsted2024dfl.com/), 'developed by DFL units in Olmsted County', also gives its recommendations for other nonpartisan races: Gabe Perkins and Michael Wojcik for Olmsted County Commissioner (Districts 2 and 6), Karen MacLaughlin for County Attorney, Pernell Meier for Soil & Water Supervisor (District 1), Jess Garcia for Mayor of Rochester, LaMar Hicks and Ruchi Gupta for City Council (Wards 3 and 5), and Cathy Nathan and Jean Marvin, with Ana Folpe, for the School Board. It writes 'No recommendation' for Soil & Water District 3 and City Council Ward 1. None of that is recorded in this file except Ana Folpe's line.

The endorsement ledger was read for leads after this part's own reading: the Kanabec County and Aitkin County DFL pages (Jeff Larson) and the state DFL's release of June 5, 2026 (Steve Simon) came from it, and each was then opened and read here. The ledger has no party page for Trent C Dilks or Joe Brothers beyond the state list, none at all for Joe McDonald, and none naming any of this part's other nonpartisan candidates. It lists the Senate District 47 DFL's site (Woodbury) as one whose certificate could not be checked, so whether that unit names Anne Burt is not known.

Nothing a card may show was found for Logan J. Kelly, Ben Livingston, Natalie Bly, Gregory Neutz, Ryan Wright and Jessica Bierwerth. Read for them: the City of Fairmont's council page and five of its board and commission pages (Kelly is on none) and the Fairmont Sentinel's report of October 1, 2026 on the mayoral candidates' forum, which names no public office for him; the City of Moorhead's candidates page and three of its board pages, and the Clay County DFL's and Republicans' candidate pages (Livingston is on none of the boards and neither party page names him); KAXE's Detroit Lakes guide of September 30, 2026, which says the sitting Ward 3 alderman is the other candidate and names no public office or website for Bly; the Crosby-Ironton district's home page and KAXE's search (nothing on Neutz); the Tri-City United district's School Board page (Wright is not among the members it names). For Judge Bierwerth no page that may be cited could be read at all: the court's and the Governor's sites are closed to this machine, no story of her appointment could be looked for without a search (Sahan Journal's search, MPR's and Bring Me The News's were tried: nothing, robots.txt, 403; the state bar association's magazine would not connect; one law school's site search was also asked for her name, and nothing is taken from it), and judgebierwerth.com exists but says only 'Launching Soon'. Joseph Banks has only his website. A second pass with web search restored would be worth it for these seven.
